subject: PrivDeploy network & CI gating review — Nexus Health readiness

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.example.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>, Alex Morris <alex.morris@nexus-health.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy network & CI gating review — Nexus Health readiness

Team —

We need a final, targeted Infrastructure-as-Code review for the Nexus Health private deployment scheduled for the end of May. Nexus is asking for a short list of gating items we must verify before we sign off: segmented VPC layout, hardened bastion/jump host, explicit egress/ingress rules, BGP/DirectConnect topology if used, CI gating (OPA/policy checks, unit-level helm/TF plan validations), and retention for audit logs (SOC2 ask).

Attached is my lightweight checklist (2027-04-13_iac-review-checklist.pdf) and the Nexus network requirements from their infra team (nexus-network-requirements.xlsx). Please review and call out:
- Any open blockers in our terraform modules (especially network/route, bastion, and egress modules)
- Missing policy checks in pipeline (OPA/Rego, Snyk, tfsec, helm-validate)
- Any ansible playbook steps that assume internal-only connectivity (we'll be in customer VPC with limited NAT)

Proposed timeline: quick round of comments today, updated PRs by Friday EOD, gated CI run early next week. Alex, looping you to make sure the scope below aligns with Nexus' expectations.

Thanks —
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy network & CI gating review — Nexus Health readiness

Kimberly — quick pass below, high-level notes (I attached a short markdown file with inline comments: irene_notes-priv-iac.md).

1) Terraform/network modules:
- vpc-module: current implementation creates public/private subnets by AZ; Nexus requires explicit management of transit subnets for their DirectConnect peer. Add a boolean flag `enable_transit_subnets` and do not auto-assign IGW on those subnets.
- route tables: we need stricter route table tagging and an explicit `no-default-route` policy for private subnets; I flagged missing `prevent_zero_cidr` guard in variables.
- bastion: the `bastion` module currently uses a generic SSH key input. Recommend adding `bastion_hardening` var to enforce SSH config (no root login, limited ciphers) and a montage of user/group mapping for audit.

2) CI gating:
- Add a pre-merge step to run `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan` with `tfsec` and `checkov` scans. Block merges when high severity results appear.
- Integrate OPA/Rego policy bundle to validate allowed egress CIDRs and deny wide-open security groups.
- Helm charts: add a `helm unit` lint + `kubeval` schema checks for CRDs and resource limits.

3) Ansible playbooks:
- Playbooks assume direct internet access for package installs; add a local package mirror option or allow `proxy` variables so Nexus air-gapped segments can pull packages.

4) Observability / Audit logging:
- Ensure terraform state locking and encrypted S3 backend with separate KMS key per customer.
- Add explicit CloudWatch/Stackdriver log export steps and retention configuration (90/180/360 day options for SOC2).

I think most items are low/medium and fixable in PRs; the transit subnet + bastion hardening are blockers for sign-off.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy network & CI gating review — Nexus Health readiness

Adding a few network/ops-specific items from the hardware/topology side:

- If Nexus is opting for Direct Connect / cross-connect, we'll need BGP ASN and VLANs defined in the TF variables. Add a `direct_connect` submodule that exposes peering BGP config as outputs for their NOC.
- For on-prem/hybrid customers, confirm whether we should enable `source/dest check` on the NLBs; for our eBPF-based LB we do asymmetric routing checks. Document the expected NAT gateway counts and fallback DMZ paths.
- HA: ensure private stacks have a minimum of two AZs and that our Terraform will fail fast if AZ quotas are insufficient.

I reviewed the proposed `priv-network` module and left inline comments in the repo (PR #428). Most changes are variable/guard additions; the main infra-level risk is around NAT scale for heavy/full model parallelism (tokens spikes).

I can take the bastion hardening task — will send a small PR with SSH config and a test playbook for kubejump access.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy network & CI gating review — Nexus Health readiness

CI/Release engineering thoughts — gating and rollout: 

- Pipeline stages we should enforce for Nexus: 1) TF fmt/validate/plan with tfsec; 2) Module unit tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform); 3) Helm lint + kubeval; 4) Integration sanity in ephemeral sandbox (small cluster emulation); 5) Canary deploy to customer dev VPC with traffic-shaping to keep model concurrency low.
- For gating, recommend `merge-blocker` status on GitHub that requires passing `policy-check` and `plan-approve` before merge. Use ephemeral creds for plan apply in sandbox — never allow long-lived creds in pipelines.
- Rollouts: prefer staged canaries with automatic rollback on error rate or latency regressions; we should wire in our tracing hooks so customer-visible SLOs are captured in the canary job.

I'll put together a skeleton GitHub Actions workflow and a sample Jenkinsfile we can reuse. Also adding a checklist of required artifacts for customer sign-off: terraform plan outputs, policy scan results, canary run logs.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Staff SRE, Release Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick review and clear notes. A couple of follow-ups from Nexus: 

- SOC2 auditors will want 1-year retention for some audit trails; can you confirm whether CloudTrail/CloudWatch exports can be configured to 365 days for our private stack?
- For package mirroring (Irene's note) — Nexus can provide an internal mirror for apt/yum. We'll provide the URL and a service account if you add a proxy-variable to the playbooks.
- Timeline: we prefer sign-off by May 6 to hit our operational window. Is that workable?

If you can confirm the SOC2 retention approach and that the bastion hardening PR will land first, Nexus will prioritize the Direct Connect provisioning (we'll send ASN/VLAN details once you confirm).

—Alex
Alex Morris
Infrastructure Lead
Nexus Health
